Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Summary 2 Fair Play 3 Links 4 Strategy Phase 5 Action Phase 5.1 Systems and Planets 5.2 Commodities and Trade Goods 5.3 Command Tokens 5.4 Strategic Action 5.5 Tactical Action 5.6 Component Action 6 Status Phase 6.1 Agenda Phase or New Game Round 7 Agenda Phase 7.1 Ready Planets 7.2 New Game Round 8 Table Host Custom Setup Summary Players optionally build a map, then play a series of game rounds. The first player to reach 10 points wins. A setup option allows playing to 14 points instead. Each game round consists of a Strategy Phase, Action Phase, Status Phase, and (possibly) Agenda Phase. Fair Play It is normal to have temporary alliances with other players in a game of Twilight Imperium 4th Edition. However, BGA terms of service forbid collusion with other users. Unfair example: 2 players should not secretly collude to play a series of games where they only attack other players. This gives an unfair advantage to manipulate their rank. Unfair example: 2 players should not secretly message each other to make deals when no one else at the table is aware of this. Fair example: A group of friends might make a Friendly Mode table, and agree at the start that they can secretly talk to each other. This way all players are on equal footing. Links Twilight Imperium: 4th Edition is a very long, complex game. This rules summary provides a basic guide, but it is highly recommended to review the official Learn to Play guide. * Learn to Play PDF * Living Rules Reference PDF * Images of all premade maps for BGA * Unofficial rules reference website Strategy Phase In clockwise order, starting with the speaker, players take turns drafting strategy cards. In 3-4 player games, each player will draft 2 strategy cards. In 5-6 player games, each player will draft 1 strategy card. If any cards are left, a trade good will be added to each one. When a player drafts a card with trade goods on it, they gain the trade goods. Action Phase In initiative order, players take turns performing actions. A player's initiative is equal to their lowest strategy card number. The lowest initiative player takes another turn after the highest initiative player takes their turn, and the Action Phase continues. Each action is either a Strategic Action, a Tactical Action, or a Component Action. If a player has used all possible Strategic Actions, they may pass and will not perform any actions for the rest of the Action Phase. However, they can play reaction cards, use reaction effects, and perform secondary abilities of strategy cards as described below. The Action Phase ends after all players have passed. Systems and Planets Each hexagon tile is a system, and each system may have 1 or more planets. Systems and planets can be clicked to examine their contents. Players can gain control of planets, which give the player an exhausted planet card matching that planet. Once the planet card becomes non-exhausted later in the game, it can be exhausted again to spend resources or influence, printed on the card, to pay various costs. Legendary planets are large planets similar to Mecatol Rex. When a player gains control of a legendary planet, they also take its legendary planet ability card. If the planet is captured for the first time, the ability card is gained in the ready state, unlike the planet card itself. If the planet is captured from another player, the ability card keeps in its current state, even if it is ready. [Rating: 1/10] This game should get a 4 like TI3, but since it's the second entry of the same game, it get's a 1.

[Rating: 1/10] Stupidly complicated "Risk" in space. No thank you. Alternate title for this could easily be "Game Setup: the Game". No game should ever force you to dedicate an entire day to playing it, but this game manages to do just that. 2 hours of said day must be set aside for setup and breakdown. How ridiculous!

[Rating: 1/10] There are too many abilities and technologies to track for both yours and opponent's which make you lost because you cannot track all of them between the game (Each players has 3 abilities and 5-10 technologies and then 5-7 action cards. OMG!!!).  Even with those ton of abilities and technologies, what you need to do in this game is trying to control nearest stars from your home base as many as possible and then build up your troops. Then sit there and vote twice a round. That's it.  I dunno why this game is rated so high. But as for me, this game is just another too much unnecessary mechanism

[Rating: 1/10] The game took 12 hours and the winner was decided by who got the most Support for the Throne cards (free victory points). Very little in the space battles most of the game is long discussions on letting each other take turns invading each other's planets.
